close_reason: Landed in 9eb89d7. Renamed Sha256::from_bytes to from_raw_digest with expanded docstring emphasising the input-vs-output distinction. Tests, PLAN.md, README.md, and lib.rs doc references updated. Workspace fmt/clippy/test/check all clean. Pre-v0.1.0 — no external consumers, no deprecation cycle needed. Note: related findings .19 (From<[u8; 32]> impl) and .20 (redundant conversion API with into_inner/From) remain open and may further reshape this surface; renaming first is forward-compatible with either resolution.
description: crate-jmap-cid-types/src/digest.rs:133 defines pub fn from_bytes(b: &[u8; 32]) -> Self that formats 32 raw SHA-256 digest bytes into the lowercase-hex wire form. The name 'from_bytes' on a type called Sha256 is a footgun: a contributor or downstream user could plausibly read 'Sha256::from_bytes(&data)' as 'compute the SHA-256 of these bytes' — the same way reqwest, sha2, ring, and md5 crates expose their hashers. They would build it (the type signature forces &[u8; 32], so they cannot pass a blob), but a wrapper or helper they write next will silently truncate or pad. Once published this rename costs a deprecation cycle. Two better names: from_digest_bytes(&[u8; 32]) or from_raw_digest(&[u8; 32]). Either makes 'this is the OUTPUT of a digest function, not the INPUT' unambiguous. Doc on the function already says 'Format 32 raw digest bytes' — pull that distinction into the name. Spec text in lib.rs/digest.rs §'This crate intentionally carries no SHA-256 computation' reinforces the design intent. Worth doing in v0.1.x before consumers fossilize the call sites.
title: Sha256::from_bytes(&[u8; 32]) name is ambiguous — reads as 'compute digest of bytes'
